items.title: Proxima Fusion bets €140M on a critical fusion ingredient dominated by Asian suppliers
items.snippet: Proxima Fusion is betting on a critical ingredient for its fusion reactors: superconducting tape. Proxima Fusion said Wednesday it plans to build a €140 million ($162.6 million) factory to produce fusion-grade high-temperature superconducting (HTS) tape, which will provide the startup with key component to its reactor design. The move comes months after Proxima raised €411 million in a round that catapulted the company up the ranks of the best-funded fusion startups. The Germany-based fusion startup plans to use a mix of public and private funding to complete the factory, with the state of Lower Saxony chipping in €21 million. Proxima will use HTS tape to generate powerful magnetic fields to contain the plasma required to spark fusion reactions. The startup’s demonstration plant will use 20,000 kilometers of HTS tape, while its commercial power plant will need twice as much. Today, the vast majority of HTS tape is made in China and Japan. HTS tape emerged a little over a decade ago as one of the fundamental breakthroughs that enabled the current generation of fusion power startups.…

items.title: Samsung reacts to Apple's foldable iPhone Duo; 'reheating our leftovers'
items.snippet: Samsung is apparently of two minds when it comes to reacting to Apple’s first foldable device, with some interesting reactions to the iPhone Duo’s unveiling, calling the device “a Sims sequel” and “reheating our leftovers.” Apple’s first foldable is official, with the iPhone Duo sharing a form factor similar to that of Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8. Samsung’s device has been very well received since its debut in July, though one could argue that the new shape was somewhat of a reaction to Apple’s imminent arrival on the scene. Chicken or egg, your choice, but Samsung’s public reaction has been quite something to watch. The foldable pioneer was welcoming to Apple ahead of the launch, but the Twitter/X feed tells another story. Samsung called the iPhone Duo a “Sim sequel” and “So far, so same,” referring to how much of what the iPhone Duo can do has been seen on existing Android foldables, including Galaxy Z Fold 8. items.title: Apple’s new iPhone camera mode promises to prove your photo isn’t AI
items.snippet: Apple is launching a new way to prove that the picture you took isn't manipulated by AI. A new feature, called "Reference Image," will arrive with the iPhone 18 Pro lineup later this month and is supposed to use the device's new camera sensor to "sign every pixel it sees." The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will only authenticate photos when placed into Reference mode. items.snippet: Obviously, part of the appeal of a foldable phone is all that additional screen real estate. items.snippet: Production theater company IMAX has responded in a mixed way to Apple's embrace of a 1:1.4 aspect ratio on the iPhone Duo's inner and outer displays. items.title: Apple Watch Ultra 4 Drops GLONASS Support
items.snippet: Apple removed GLONASS support from the Apple Watch Ultra 4 , according to technical specifications listed for the device. The Ultra 4 supports GPS, Galileo, QZSS, and BeiDou, while the prior-generation Ultra 3 supported GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, QZSS, and BeiDou. GPS, Galileo, BeiDou, and QZSS use CDMA-based signaling and support multiple frequencies for more accurate positioning. Consumer devices typically only receive an L1 signal from GLONASS, so it is less useful on devices with dual-frequency support. GLONASS also uses a different signal architecture, and receivers have to correct for hardware timing delays on a per-satellite basis, which can lead to positioning errors. Apple did not say w

John Ternus (left) and Greg Joswiak - image credit: Tom's Guide/TechRadar It had been rumored for such a long time, and so many leaks got little details right, but overall the iPhone Duo has been Apple's best-kept secret in years. Talking to Tom's Guide and TechRadar in a new interview , Greg Joswiak , senior vice president of worldwide marketing, says he's "super proud" of that. Apple has no control over what countries choose to name a location The United States President has begun using the names on the map as some kind of negotiating tactic in ongoing trade wars he started. After executive orders changed The Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario in the GNIS database, Apple Maps reflected that change. items.title: No, you won't be able to play two videos at once on iPhone Duo
items.snippet: There are two displays and multitasking options for iPhone Duo, but that doesn't mean you'll be able to play two videos at the same time. iPhone Duo has two displays If you've ever been scrolling a social media app while listening to music, you've likely had the frustrating experience of having the music pause randomly. That's because the social media app took over as the primary audio provider. The same effect occurs whenever you're watching video on iPhone or iPad . Picture-in-picture, split view, or even dual screens won't let a user play two videos at once, even on iPhone Duo. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

Every data point that can be included will help provide a holistic view of your health, but not everyone has ease of access to medical labs. items.title: Decision time: iPhone Duo vs iPhone 18 Pro & iPad mini
items.snippet: Apple has finally announced the iPhone Duo after years of guesswork, and it immediately replaced the idea of an iPad mini for a whole lot of people. There's a good argument for an iPhone 18 Pro and iPad mini instead, for less money. Apple's iPhone Duo opens up to a size similar to iPad mini Open, the iPhone Duo has a 7.6-inch OLED display that is just a few tenths of an inch smaller than the current iPad mini's 8.3-inch IPS display. The iPhone Duo also has the added benefit of folding up when you don't need it, making it eminently more pocketable. That alone is enough to make some people throw their iPad mini to the curb. That may be the case for you, too, but the iPhone Duo isn't perfect. A

items.snippet: I had a lot of reservations about Apple making a foldable iPhone, but after playing around with iPhone Duo at the Apple Event , I think I'm sold. That was before I got the chance to try it out for myself. It wasn't long, but in my time with it, I can easily see it being my daily driver. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

items.snippet: Apple's newly announced iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo both use a new A20 Pro chip, and it could be the key to Siri AI taking the step from being full of potential to being the game-changer we were promised. Siri AI is coming Siri AI has been part of Apple's iOS 27 beta testing process since its June WWDC debut. It's also available in Apple's beta software across its other hardware platforms. It'll be available to the public on all of those platforms before the end of September. But Siri AI itself will remain a beta feature for the foreseeable future. items.title: Apple is laying groundwork for ads in Visual Intelligence
items.snippet: Apple could be looking to squeeze a little more advertising into the iPhone , this time through Visual Intelligence. Apple may allow sponsored content within Visual Intelligence Visual Intelligence may eventually support sponsored results from search providers like Google, allowing advertising to appear alongside regular search results. The change appears to be part of Apple's upcoming iOS 27 . Aaron Perris discovered the code within iOS 27. He notes that it would support sponsored images similar to those already appearing on similar services. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

items.title: Why your iPhone Duo will inevitably develop a screen crease
items.snippet: The iPhone Duo developing a crease over time is inevitable as the tides, and a matter of physics and engineering. Here's how and why that crease develops, and what Apple has done to mitigate it. iPhone Duo glass layers In the run-up to Apple's folding iPhone, there was a lot of chatter about how Apple has "solved the smartphone crease." It's always been a silly topic, as there is no solving it, there is only postponing it. It's an engineering problem on top of a physics problem. The physics are immutable. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

items.title: iPhone Duo is typical Apple - never first, usually best
items.snippet: Apple has been practically mocked for how many years it has taken for it to release a foldable iPhone , but yet again it's proven it knew what it was doing all along. It took 15 years from the patent on the left to the iPhone Duo on the right - images credit: Apple. Think of the iPhone . Or the iPod, the Mac , the iPad , AirPods , AirTags , the Apple Watch ... Actually, try to think of anything where Apple was actually first to market. Apple wasn't even the first company to make a laptop Mac. To even arguably find a product Apple made first, you have to go back to the Apple II. Even then, as revolutionary as it was, there had been computers before it. items.title: iPhone Duo users can be authenticated with Apple Watch if Touch ID isn't ideal
items.snippet: Face ID wasn't going to work on iPhone Duo, so Apple chose Touch ID instead. For those that don't like Touch ID, Apple Watch will authenticate them automatically. Apple chose a Touch ID sensor for iPhone Duo since Face ID would have proven difficult The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable device , which means it can be used opened or closed. Apple couldn't find a way to make Face ID work in both use cases, so it offered Touch ID instead. The benefit of Touch ID on a foldable is that it can be authenticated no matter if the device is open or closed, or facing forward or backward. items.snippet: Apple has confirmed that macOS 27 Golden Gate will arrive on September 14 with iOS 27, bringing a sizable collection of new features and improvements to the Mac. items.snippet: Alongside the $1,999 iPhone Duo price, Apple has also increased the price of every older model it still sells including the aging iPhone 16 by $100 as ongoing component shortages continue to bite. items.title: Contrary to early rumors, iPhone Duo does have MagSafe charging
items.snippet: The rumor mill has gone back and forth about a lot of things about the folding iPhone , but we're happy to report that the iPhone Duo does, in fact, have MagSafe charging. MagSafe is on the iPhone Duo, on the non-screen side under the camera Of all the things to talk about, Apple chose to leave out if the iPhone Duo had MagSafe . We understand, it makes sense if you don't want to have a two-hour keynote about it. Fortunately, Apple's technical specs are clear about it. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

items.title: It's going to be a while before you can pre-order an iPhone Duo
items.snippet: Apple's iPhone 18 Pro event is over. You're going to have to wait until October to pre-order and use the iPhone Duo. Apple's iPhone Duo, in action We suspected from the beginning that the folding iPhone wasn't going to arrive day-and-date as the iPhone 18 Pro would. We missed our early guesses on when, though. Reminiscent of the iPhone X, Apple says that pre-orders for iPhone Duo start at 8 AM ET on Friday, October 16. Availability begins on Friday, October 23. items.title: See the crowd go wild for John Ternus with his iPhone Duo reveal
items.snippet: Apple's famous "one more thing" returned as John Ternus unveiled the iPhone Duo, giving his first event as CEO a crowd-pleasing echo of the Steve Jobs era. iPhone Duo Ternus appeared ready to close the event before pausing to deliver the familiar phrase. The Steve Jobs Theater audience immediately erupted as the presentation turned to Apple's long-awaited foldable iPhone. Steve Jobs made "one more thing" synonymous with Apple's biggest surprises, using it to introduce products and features the company deliberately held until the end. Tim Cook later revived the line sparingly for major launches, including Apple Watch and iPhone X. Subscribe to AppleInsider on YouTube Continue Reading on Apple

items.title: Apple Watch Ultra 4 is here with a faster chip and improved battery life
items.snippet: Apple's high-end smartwatch just got a massive performance boost, as the Apple Watch Ultra 4 now boasts the powerful S11 chip. Apple Watch Ultra 4 is here. On Wednesday, alongside the long-awaited iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, the Apple Watch Ultra 4 made its debut. The new model is somewhat of a spec-bump upgrade, offering improved battery life with the same tried-and-true design. items.title: China-modified Nvidia RTX 5090 with massive 96GB of memory appears on Alibaba for less than $4,000 — 3x more VRAM at 65% the cost of the original
items.snippet: An alleged Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 96GB with 96GB of modded VRAM surfaces on Alibaba for $3888.

items.title: Sanctioned Chinese supercomputer maker stripped of IO500 benchmark crown, Intel-powered Aurora retakes the lead — record-breaking ParaStor F9000 storage system doesn't meet reproducibility requirements
items.snippet: Sugon's record-breaking ParaStor F9000 storage systems have lost their IO500 Production crowns and have been moved to the Research list after failing to meet the benchmark's highest reproducibility requirements, which include widely available architecture details and general availability of hardware itself.

items.title: Save 20% on this 144-in-1 screwdriver set, perfect for hobbyists and PC builders under $40 — epic starter toolkit ships with electric and precision drivers, along with 120 magnetic bits and 22 maintenance tools
items.snippet: This 144-in-1 repair toolkit from Strebito is on sale, with 120 bits and a number of other tools for less than $40.

items.title: GameStop is reopening recently closed stores despite massive retail cuts — select locations return nationwide starting September 11
items.snippet: After shutting down hundreds of locations and dramatically shrinking its physical retail footprint, GameStop is bringing select stores back as its business continues to evolve beyond physical games.

items.title: Hardware-accurate NeoGeo AES+ delayed to late 2027 due to memory shortage — decision driven by surging demand and AI-driven RAM crunch
items.snippet: NeoGeo AES+ console remake delayed for nearly a year — decision driven by RAM shortage and unexpected popularity

items.title: Hands On: Sharge's Disk Pro 2 Ultra is a compact, magnetic DIY SSD dock with active cooling, 80W passthrough charging, and HDMI 2.1, supporting up to 8TB drives
items.snippet: One of our favorite external SSDs gets an upgrade as a compact DIY hub with an M.2 slot, active cooling, USB ports, up to HDMI 2.1, and a removable cable.

items.title: Desktop graphics card shipments hit four-year high of 12.5 million despite increasing prices — Nvidia takes 90% share as gamers rush to beat looming price spikes
items.snippet: Shipments of desktop add-in-boards in Q2 were the highest since Q1 2022 despite rising prices and dropping sales of desktop PCs, according to new numbers from Jon Peddie Research.

items.title: Snag a huge $1,000 saving on this RTX 5090 OLED gaming laptop from HP, now $3,699 — 16-inch HyperX rig delivers 1600p gaming with ultra-fast 240Hz refresh rate, coupled with 32GB DDR5 RAM and a 2TB SSD
items.snippet: The HyperX Omen Max 16, featuring the powerful Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 GPU, is down to $3,699.99 right now, saving you $1,000.

items.title: AMD releases new Ryzen 5 5500F and Ryzen 5 7500 for budget PC builders — new budget Zen 3 and Zen 4 CPUs soften the blow from high RAM prices
items.snippet: AMD has officially launched the Ryzen 5 5500F and Ryzen 5 7500 processors with six Zen 3 and Zen 4 cores, respectively.

items.title: Apple’s new A20 Pro smartphone chip around 25% faster than its predecessor in leaked benchmark — the 2nm CPU in the iPhone Duo and 18 Pro hits nearly 5 GHz clocks
items.snippet: The first Apple A20 Geekbench 6 benchmark results are starting to pop up online and the single-core score is very impressive.

items.title: Libernovo Omni Pro Review: Cooler than you think
items.snippet: Libernovo's Omni Pro is a dynamic, ergonomic gaming chair with motorized lumbar support and a ventilation fan that works surprisingly well.

items.title: Old MacBook uses a mirror, webcam, and AI agent to code its own AMD GPU drivers — 'agent-first' Omarchy Linux debugs itself, AI can check its own progress on screen in real-time
items.snippet: Using an 'age of agents' Linux distro a 'MacBook is using its webcam to look at its screen in a mirror to improve AMD Radeon chip support.'

items.title: China's AI accelerator supplier Biren posts 2,000% year-over-year revenue growth — US export controls benefit homegrown chips as Nvidia and AMD exit market
items.snippet: Biren Technology shows unprecedented shipments growth in 1H 2026 as competition from AMD and Nvidia vanishes (at least officially).

items.title: Chinese quartz approved for semiconductor equipment and DRAM manufacturing, but it still can't break America's monopoly — China secures domestic supply for chipmaking components, but Spruce Pine still holds the crucible monopoly
items.snippet: Pacific Quartz gets its high-purity quartz qualified for semiconductor equipment and DRAM manufacturing.

items.title: Modded RTX 5090 ditches 16-pin power for triple 8-pin connectors — draws up to 900W and hits 3,400 MHz
items.snippet: TecLab’s experiment puts the humble 8-pin connector to an extreme test, with the modified RTX 5090 pulling more than 120A while avoiding the newer 12V-2x6 design altogether.

items.title: TSMC, Samsung, and Intel shore up support with ASML to deploy larger High-NA EUV photomasks — 6×12-inch photomask transition may take years despite unified effort
items.snippet: ASML, Intel, Samsung, and TSMC back development of 6×12-inch to build large processors using High-NA EUV lithography systems without stitching.

items.title: Developer uses Claude to vibe code a Windows 3.1 shell in an hour — reanimated 12MB retro launcher runs on both Windows 11 and Apple Silicon
items.snippet: There’s a new vibe-coded clone of the Windows 3.1 Program Manager that runs on modern Windows 11 or macOS systems.

items.title: Save $250 on this 1080p-ready gaming laptop with an RTX 5060, now just $1049 — MSI Cyborg 15 rig ships with a 15.6-inch 144Hz display, 16GB DDR5 RAM, and an eight-core Intel CPU
items.snippet: This MSI gaming laptop is fit for 1080p gaming, thanks to an RTX 5060, with $250 off knocking the price down to just $1049.99.

items.title: Intel-backed auto-overclocking tool Hypertune optimizes individual systems, not test profiles — tool claims FPS improvement of up to 60% on Intel-based systems
items.snippet: Hypertune is an automated overclocking tool built on top of Intel's Extreme Tuning Utility (XTU) SDK and built in collaboration with engineers at Intel.

items.title: Framework cuts 32GB and 64GB memory prices for new Laptop 13 Pro, issues retroactive refunds — modular laptop maker secures 'limited quantity' of LPCAMM2 RAM at lower cost
items.snippet: Modular laptop maker Framework is dropping some of its memory pricing, including for some already-shipped orders, in a piece of good news for consumers.

items.title: Goodram PX700 2TB SSD Review: High-end punch on a budget core
items.snippet: The Goodram PX700 matches good all-around performance with high power-efficiency in a cool-running package. It performs mostly like a premium drive, although pricing remains a concern.

items.title: OpenAI claims GPT-6 Astra is an ethereal 'Alien Mind' with AGI-like qualities — company warns of alignment challenges as new frontier leader emerges
items.snippet: OpenAI has made bold claims with its new GPT-6 Astra AI model, and it's certainly capable, but benchmarks suggest it has many of the usual weaknesses alongside the strengths, while cost and accessibility are still the biggest factors in widespread usage.

items.title: This $502 4TB Crucial T705 is the cheapest Gen 5 SSD you can buy right now for just 12.5 cents per GB — ultra-fast storage upgrade with unreal 14,500 MB/s speeds is $181 less than a month ago, hitting its lowest price since February
items.snippet: Save 10% on this 4TB Crucial T705 SSD, the cheapest Gen 5 4TB SSD on the market by some distance at the moment, now just $502.51.

items.title: Nvidia's unreleased RTX 3070 Ti 16GB comes to life thanks to a modder's crazy GDDR6 swap — Frankenstein card combines RTX 3070 PCB and new VRAM with RTX 3070 Ti GPU
items.snippet: A modder has recreated the never-released RTX 3070 Ti with 16GB of VRAM using GDDR6 chips instead of the GDDR6X the retail 3070 Ti actually shipped with.

items.title: Chuwi UniBox AI495 Pro looks a bit like the old Mac Pro and, with 192GB RAM, matches Apple's new workstation for memory

items.title: Leap second proposal will keep software stacks in sync
items.snippet: For decades, global time experts have mapped atomic clock time to the earth’s rotation, periodically adding a second (aka a leap second) as rotation slowed. But the planet’s rotation has now slightly sped up, which could mean that a negative adjustment will be required. The problem is that computer systems have not been programmed to do that. To avoid this issue, the General Conference on Weights and Measures (GCWM) in October will vote on a proposal to maintain the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) as a continuous time from May 20, 2027, without adjustment via leap seconds, allowing UT1 , the measure of time based on the earth’s rotation, and UTC to drift apart by up to one hour. items.title: Network complexity is outpacing NetOps teams: How AI can help
items.snippet: Network infrastructure owners often tell me that the biggest obstacle to network cyber resilience is the complexity of multi-vendor network environments. They aren’t just referring to the number of vendors in their environment, but also to the variety of device types (firewalls, routers, switches and access points), models and software versions. Well-resourced organizations with vendor-specific expertise on their NetOps team can usually manage three to five vendors at most. Beyond that, the talent, skill and training required to handle greater complexity are often beyond their reach. items.title: Nvidia invests $3.5B in MediaTek to extend its grip on AI
items.snippet: Nvidia continues to commit major dollars to AI companies, this time investing $3.5 billion in chipmaker MediaTek in return for licensing Nvidia technology. Nvidia will purchase $3.5 billion of convertible bonds issued by chipmaker MediaTek, and in return MediaTek will adopt Nvidia’s NVLink Fusion technology , allowing customers to develop customized AI accelerators that can connect directly to Nvidia-based AI infrastructure. items.title: MikroTik patches flaws currently being exploited to take over routers
items.snippet: Networking gear manufacturer MikroTik has released patches for six vulnerabilities in its RouterOS firmware, two of which can be chained together to take over devices without authentication over SSH. The exploit chain, dubbed MikroTrick, is already being used by attackers in the wild. items.title: Cisco bundles fixes for multiple vulnerabilities, some critical, into one patch
items.snippet: Cisco is looking to get ahead of attackers with a new set of more than a half-dozen fixes, some of them critical, for its IOS XR Linux-based network operating system (OS). As part of its regular testing, Cisco’s software engineering team flagged “multiple internally-discovered vulnerabilities ,” the company said. These flaws could allow attackers to perform remote code execution (RCE) and gain root access on a router, thereby allowing them to intercept traffic. Other potential risks could include access control failures, buffer overflows, and out-of-bounds access. Cisco said all IOS XR releases, including IOS XR7, are impacted, regardless of configuration.
